_law: ONLY SHRINKS. Every row is a <path>:<line> citation in a LIVE document whose line is PAST THE END of the file it addresses — an address that cannot be right, whatever it meant to name. A citation not listed here FAILS tests/lint/sourceCitationIntegrity.walker.test.js; a listed row that has gone also fails, with 'delete its entry', so the set can only fall. It holds the SET, never counts: a count assertion would red every time a doc legitimately re-states an address it already carries, and a gate that reds on correct behaviour gets turned off. THE DOOR: re-address the citation to the symbol it names and DELETE its row. A row is NEVER silenced by editing a document's path into the archival rule — that rule is measured and listed in the walker's header.
_door: To clear a row: open the citing document, find the symbol the sentence names, locate it in the target, write the true line, delete the row here. To add one: you cannot — a new past-EOF citation in a live document is a RED, not a baseline entry. src/, tests/ and scripts/ have NO baseline at all: past-EOF there is always red.
